question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tool confirmation gate, and which deterministic risk/current-turn authorization semantics should decide allow, require-confirm, deny, and timeout behavior?
rationale: This changes the core authorization boundary for model-proposed writes, exec, messages, gateway actions, and credential-bearing calls; source inspection can prove the gap, but not the product/security policy maintainers want.

options.title: Design core gate
options.body: Approve a maintainer-led core design that adds a disabled-by-default confirmation config, deterministic tool risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout semantics, and regression coverage around existing plugin approvals.

options.title: Restrict to plugin seam
options.body: Keep core behavior unchanged and require operators to implement contextual approval through before_tool_call.requireApproval or trusted tool policies, accepting that no built-in same-response confirmation gate exists.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Leave this issue open but defer implementation until related action-level deny, HITL interrupt, and response-gate policy work settles into one authorization model.

recommendation.title: Design core gate
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-led core design that adds a disabled-by-default confirmation config, deterministic tool risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout semantics, and regression coverage around existing plugin approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans security defaults, config surface, and the agent-core execution loop, and recent product/security review plus runtime extraction history makes this the best available routing owner.
